title: Morphisms of coherent formal modules whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of an ideal
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme, $\mathcal I,\mathcal K\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ quasi-coherent sheaves of ideals and $\alpha=(\alpha_n):(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ a morphism of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ with $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde I$, $\mathcal K|_U=\widetilde K$ ($I=\mathcal I(U)$, $K=\mathcal K(U)$), let $\alpha_U:M\to N$ be the $A^\wedge$-linear map of finitely generated $A^\wedge$-modules ($A^\wedge$ the $I$-adic completion) $M=\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n(U)\to N=\varprojlim_n\mathcal G_n(U)$, $\alpha_U=\varprojlim_n\alpha_n(U)$, which corresponds to $\alpha|_U$ under the equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2). The following are equivalent: (1) there is $t\ge1$ such that $\mathcal K^t\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_n)=0$ and $\mathcal K^t\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha_n)=0$ for all $n\ge1$ (kernels and cokernels of $\mathcal O_X$-modules); (2) for every affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ there is $t\ge1$ with $K^t\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_U)=0$ and $K^t\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha_U)=0$; (3) there are a finite covering $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_r$ by affine opens and $t\ge1$ such that the condition of (2) holds for every $\alpha_{U_i}$; (4) there is $t\ge1$ such that the kernel and the cokernel of $\alpha$ in the abelian category $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian] are annihilated by $\mathcal K^t$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (3). (Stacks then says that $\alpha$ is a map whose kernel and cokernel are annihilated by a power of $\mathcal K$.) Moreover, the integer $t$ of (1) may be replaced by $2t$ when passing from (3) to (1), and the commutative algebra fact behind this holds: if $0\to T\to M\xrightarrow{u}N\to Q\to0$ is an exact sequence of modules over a ring $A$ with $K^tT=K^tQ=0$, then for every ideal $J\subseteq A$ the kernel and cokernel of $u\bmod J:M/JM\to N/JN$ are annihilated by $K^{2t}$.

proof.text: (Setup on an affine open.) Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $A=\mathcal O_X(U)$, so $(U,\mathcal O_X|_U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; $A$ is Noetherian since $X$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-affine-open-locnoeth]. Put $I=\mathcal I(U)$, $K=\mathcal K(U)$; as $\mathcal I|_U,\mathcal K|_U$ are quasi-coherent, the counits $\widetilde I\to\mathcal I|_U$, $\widetilde K\to\mathcal K|_U$ are isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3), so the hypothesis $\mathcal I|_U=\widetilde I$, $\mathcal K|_U=\widetilde K$ of the statement holds for every affine open. The restriction $\rho_U:\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)\to\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)$ is a well-defined additive functor [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-local-exactness] (1), and $E_U:\mathit{Coh}(U,\mathcal I|_U)\to\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A^\wedge)$, $(\mathcal H_n)\mapsto\varprojlim_n\mathcal H_n(U)$, is an equivalence [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (2). So $M=E_U(\rho_U(\mathcal F_n))=\varprojlim\mathcal F_n(U)$, $N=\varprojlim\mathcal G_n(U)$ and $\alpha_U=E_U(\rho_U\alpha)=\varprojlim\alpha_n(U)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (1) the projections $p_n:M\to\mathcal F_n(U)$, $q_n:N\to\mathcal G_n(U)$ are surjective with kernels $I^nM$, $I^nN$ (the $A$-submodules generated by the $am$, $a\in I^n$), and $\alpha_n(U)\circ p_n=q_n\circ\alpha_U$ by the definition of $\varprojlim\alpha_n(U)$. Hence, regarding $M,N$ as $A$-modules through $A\to A^\wedge$ (so $K^tM$, $I^nM$ are the $A$-submodules generated by products), the isomorphisms $M/I^nM\cong\mathcal F_n(U)$, $N/I^nN\cong\mathcal G_n(U)$ induced by $p_n,q_n$ identify $\alpha_n(U)$ with $\bar u_n=\alpha_U\bmod I^n:M/I^nM\to N/I^nN$, compatibly with the transition maps; in particular $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_n(U)\cong\operatorname{Ker}\bar u_n$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n(U)\cong\operatorname{Coker}\bar u_n$ as $A$-modules. Moreover the canonical map $M\to\varprojlim_nM/I^nM$ is bijective: followed by the bijection $\varprojlim_nM/I^nM\to\varprojlim_n\mathcal F_n(U)$ induced by the $p_n$, it is $x\mapsto(p_n(x))_n$, the identity of $M=\varprojlim\mathcal F_n(U)$; likewise for $N$.

Then ... Ker(M/I^nM -> N/I^nN) ...')

proof.text: (Annihilation is checked on affine opens.) Let $\mathcal H$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module and $t\ge1$. Then $\mathcal K^t\mathcal H$ is quasi-coherent and $(\mathcal K^t\mathcal H)(U)=\mathcal K(U)^t\mathcal H(U)$ for every affine open $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-times-quasi-coherent-affine-sections] (1),(2). Hence $\mathcal K^t\mathcal H=0$ implies $\mathcal K(U)^t\mathcal H(U)=0$ for every affine open $U$; conversely, if $\mathcal K(U_i)^t\mathcal H(U_i)=0$ for the members of some affine open covering $X=\bigcup U_i$, then $(\mathcal K^t\mathcal H)|_{U_i}$ is a quasi-coherent module on the affine scheme $U_i$ with zero global sections, hence zero (its counit $\widetilde 0\to(\mathcal K^t\mathcal H)|_{U_i}$ is an isomorphism, [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction] (3)), so $\mathcal K^t\mathcal H=0$. Apply this to $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_n$, quasi-coherent [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] with $(\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_n)(U)=\operatorname{Ker}(\alpha_n(U))$ (kernels are sectionwise), and to $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n$, quasi-coherent with $(\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n)(U)=\operatorname{Coker}(\alpha_n(U))$ for affine $U$ [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (2),(3); by Step 0 these are $\operatorname{Ker}\bar u_n$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\bar u_n$. Conclusion: for $t\ge1$ and any affine open covering $X=\bigcup U_i$ the following are equivalent: (1) holds with $t$; (1') for every affine open $U$ and every $n$, $K^t$ annihilates $\operatorname{Ker}(\bar u_n)$ and $\operatorname{Coker}(\bar u_n)$, where $\bar u_n=\alpha_U\bmod I^n$; (1'') the same for the $U_i$.

proof.text: ((3) implies (1), with $2t$.) Let $X=U_1\cup\dots\cup U_r$ and $t$ be as in (3), and write $A_i,I_i,K_i$ and $\alpha_{U_i}:M_i\to N_i$ as in Step 0. For each $i$ apply [lem-weil-pbc-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-mod-ideal] (c) over the ring $A_i$, with the ideal $K_i$, the map $u=\alpha_{U_i}$ (an $A_i$-linear map of $A_i$-modules with $K_i^t\operatorname{Ker}u=K_i^t\operatorname{Coker}u=0$) and $J=I_i^n$: the kernel and the cokernel of $\bar u_n=\alpha_{U_i}\bmod I_i^n$ are annihilated by $K_i^{2t}$, for every $n$. By Step 1 ((1'')$\Rightarrow$(1)) condition (1) holds with $2t$. This also proves the clause 'the integer $t$ may be replaced by $2t$ when passing from (3) to (1)', and the commutative algebra fact of the statement is [lem-weil-pbc-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-mod-ideal] (c).

proof.text: ((1) implies (2), with $2t$ for every $U$.) Let (1) hold with $t$ and let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine open, with $\alpha_U:M\to N$ as in Step 0. By Step 1 ((1)$\Rightarrow$(1')), $K^t$ annihilates $\operatorname{Ker}\bar u_n$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\bar u_n$ for every $n$. Fix $f,g\in K^t$ and let $h_n:N/I^nN\to M/I^nM$ be the map $h_{f,g}$ of [lem-weil-pbc-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-mod-ideal] (a) for $\bar u_n$ (over the ring $A$, ideal $K$). The reductions $\pi:M/I^{n+1}M\to M/I^nM$, $\pi:N/I^{n+1}N\to N/I^nN$ satisfy $\bar u_n\circ\pi=\pi\circ\bar u_{n+1}$, so by the naturality (b) there, $h_n\circ\pi=\pi\circ h_{n+1}$: the $h_n$ form a map of inverse systems and induce an $A$-linear $\varprojlim h_n:\varprojlim N/I^nN\to\varprojlim M/I^nM$; composing with the bijections of Step 0 ($N\cong\varprojlim N/I^nN$, $M\cong\varprojlim M/I^nM$) gives an $A$-linear $h:N\to M$ with $h(y)\bmod I^nM=h_n(y\bmod I^nN)$ for all $n$. For $x\in M$, $h(\alpha_U(x))\bmod I^n=h_n(\bar u_n(x\bmod I^n))=fg\,x\bmod I^n$ for all $n$ ([lem-weil-pbc-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-mod-ideal] (a)), so $h\circ\alpha_U=fg\cdot\mathrm{id}_M$ by the injectivity of $M\to\varprojlim M/I^nM$; likewise $\alpha_U\circ h=fg\cdot\mathrm{id}_N$. As $f,g\in K^t$ were arbitrary, [lem-weil-pbc-kernel-cokernel-annihilated-mod-ideal] (d) (with $v=\alpha_U$) shows that $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_U$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_U$ are annihilated by $K^{2t}$. So (2) holds, even with the same exponent $2t$ for every affine open $U$.

proof.text: ((2) implies (3).) $X$ is locally Noetherian, so it has a covering by affine opens [pqf-def-locnoeth], and its underlying space is quasi-compact, so finitely many of them, $U_1,\dots,U_r$, cover $X$. By (2) there are $t_i\ge1$ with $K_i^{t_i}$ annihilating $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_{U_i}$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_{U_i}$; with $t=\max_it_i$ we have $K_i^t\subseteq K_i^{t_i}$, so (3) holds with this covering and $t$.

proof.text: (Kernel and cokernel in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ on an affine open.) $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ is abelian [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-abelian]; let $\iota:(\mathcal H_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)$ be a kernel and $c:(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal C_n)$ a cokernel of $\alpha$ (by that node one may take $\mathcal C_n=\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_n$; kernels and cokernels are unique up to isomorphism, and an isomorphism $(\mathcal H_n)\cong(\mathcal H'_n)$ has isomorphisms as components, which carry $\mathcal K^t\mathcal H_n$ onto $\mathcal K^t\mathcal H'_n$ (each component maps $\mathcal K^t\mathcal H_n$ into $\mathcal K^t\mathcal H'_n$, since an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map sends a local section $\sum a_is_i$, $a_i\in\mathcal K^t$, to $\sum a_i\varphi(s_i)$; notation of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (0); and so does its inverse), so condition (4) does not depend on the choice). Let $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ be an affine open, notation of Step 0, and put $T=\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_U\subseteq M$, $Q=N/\alpha_U(M)$. The functor $\rho_U$ is exact [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-local-exactness] (1), so $\rho_U(\iota)$ is a kernel and $\rho_U(c)$ a cokernel of $\rho_U(\alpha)$ [lem-sp-exact-functor-preserves-homology] (a). The equivalence $E_U$ carries kernels to kernels and cokernels to cokernels (the universal property is transported: $E_U$ is fully faithful and every object of $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A^\wedge)$ is isomorphic to one in its image). In $\mathrm{Mod}^{fg}(A^\wedge)$ the inclusion $T\subseteq M$ is a kernel and $N\to Q$ a cokernel of $\alpha_U$: $A^\wedge$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], so the submodule $T$ of the finitely generated $M$ and the quotient $Q$ of $N$ are finitely generated [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and the universal properties are those of the module kernel and cokernel. Hence $E_U(\rho_U(\mathcal H_n))\cong T$ and $E_U(\rho_U(\mathcal C_n))\cong Q$ as $A^\wedge$-modules. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-modules-affine] (1) to $\rho_U(\mathcal H_n)$ and $\rho_U(\mathcal C_n)$ as in Step 0: $\mathcal H_n(U)\cong T/I^nT$ and $\mathcal C_n(U)\cong Q/I^nQ$ as $A$-modules for every $n$, and the canonical maps $T\to\varprojlim_nT/I^nT$, $Q\to\varprojlim_nQ/I^nQ$ are bijective; in particular $\bigcap_nI^nT=0$ and $\bigcap_nI^nQ=0$.

proof.text: ((4) is equivalent to (2) with one exponent for all $U$, and to (3); end of the proof.) Let $t\ge1$. The $\mathcal H_n$ and $\mathcal C_n$ are coherent, hence quasi-coherent [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]. For an affine open $U$, Step 5 gives $K^t\mathcal H_n(U)\cong K^t(T/I^nT)=(K^tT+I^nT)/I^nT$; so $K^t\mathcal H_n(U)=0$ for all $n$ iff $K^tT\subseteq\bigcap_nI^nT=0$, i.e. iff $K^tT=0$; likewise $K^t\mathcal C_n(U)=0$ for all $n$ iff $K^tQ=0$. By Step 1 (applied to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal H_n$, $\mathcal C_n$), $(\mathcal H_n)$ and $(\mathcal C_n)$ are annihilated by $\mathcal K^t$ in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] (3) iff $K^t$ annihilates $\operatorname{Ker}\alpha_U$ and $\operatorname{Coker}\alpha_U$ for every affine open $U$, iff it does so for the members $U_i$ of one (any) affine open covering. Hence (4) with $t$ implies (2) (with $t$ for every $U$), and (3) with $t$ implies (4) with $t$. Together with Steps 2-4 ((3)$\Rightarrow$(1)$\Rightarrow$(2)$\Rightarrow$(3)) the four conditions are equivalent.
